articles.title: Welcome to the APL Hackathon
articles.summary: What to expect at the Attleboro Public Library’s monthly hackathon — no experience required, just curiosity.
articles.lede: What to expect at our monthly meetup on North Main Street — no experience required, just curiosity.

articles.title: Why You Should Bring a Friend
articles.summary: Hackathons are better together. Tips for inviting someone who has never coded before.
articles.lede: Hackathons are better together — especially for first-timers.

articles.title: Library Wi‑Fi, Power Outlets, and Quiet Corners
articles.summary: A practical guide to working comfortably in the Attleboro Public Library {location}.
articles.lede: Settle in for a productive — and comfortable — {meetupDay}.

themes.title: Games from Scratch
themes.summary: Recreate a classic game with a small scope, or stretch into Pong, Snake, and arcade clones.
themes.lede: Visual feedback and quick demos — pick a light or heavy track and ship something playable.
themes.bannerText: Finish a tiny game in one session, then add stretch features if you have time.

themes.title: Data for Good
themes.summary: Turn public datasets into charts, maps, and civic questions about the places we live.
themes.lede: Prefer one dataset and a few focused questions over a sprawling dashboard.
themes.bannerText: Transit, parks, weather, census — tell a clear story with open data.

themes.title: Automate Your Life
themes.summary: Write a short script that does one repetitive job reliably — files, weather, bots, and more.
themes.lede: Personal tools, bots, and file chores. Start with a dry-run.
themes.bannerText: Pick one annoying task and automate the happy path first.

themes.title: The Interactive Story
themes.summary: Branching stories, Twine, p5.js, and visual novels — writing and code in the same room.
themes.lede: Great for mixed groups: storytellers and programmers can pair up.
themes.bannerText: Outline endings first, then wire up choices, inventory, and a little state.

themes.title: API Mashup
themes.summary: Fetch JSON from public APIs, then combine two services into one coherent product.
themes.lede: From a joke button to an ISS soundtrack — request, parse, display.
themes.bannerText: Get one API working end-to-end before you style or mash anything up.

themes.title: Library Tech
themes.summary: Events pages, digital signage, reservations, and catalog companions for library life.
themes.lede: Staff-facing and patron-facing prototypes — label demos clearly.
themes.bannerText: Ship something that looks intentional on a phone and a desktop.

themes.title: Creative Pokédex Design
themes.summary: Build a Pokédex-style viewer with PokéAPI or original creatures and a strong visual theme.
themes.lede: List, detail, search, and type badges — then treat it as a design system.
themes.bannerText: Fan / educational / unofficial — credit PokéAPI and prefer original creatures when you can.

themes.title: Trick-or-Treat Map
themes.summary: Find which houses in Attleboro are handing out candy — a neighborhood map for Halloween.
themes.lede: Local maps and community data for trick-or-treaters in Attleboro, MA.
themes.bannerText: Help neighbors find participating houses and plan a walking route.

themes.title: Git for Beginners
themes.summary: First commit, branches, and pull requests — practice on the Hello-World repo.
themes.lede: Leave with a working mental model and a real commit on GitHub.
themes.bannerText: Read git status before every other command. Pair with the Git tutorial page.

themes.title: Build a Website
themes.summary: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript — ship a real page, then stretch into a small multi-section site.
themes.lede: From a single landing page to a tiny portfolio or meetup homepage. Structure first, style second, interactivity last.
themes.bannerText: Finish something you can open in a browser. Pair with the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript tutorials if you want a warm-up.

tutorials.title: Using the Terminal
tutorials.summary: Navigate folders, write a small shell script, and make a Git commit — beginner and advanced tracks.
tutorials.lede: This session’s goal. Pick the beginner track or the advanced track and work the steps in order.

tutorials.title: HTML
tutorials.summary: Headings, links, forms, and semantic structure — the bones of every webpage.
tutorials.lede: Start with MDN and Learn HTML in Y Minutes, then practice with small interactive drills.

tutorials.title: CSS
tutorials.summary: Colors, typography, flexbox, grid, and responsive layout for your HTML.
tutorials.lede: Learn by doing: CSS Diner, Flexbox Froggy, and Grid Garden are the community favorites.

tutorials.title: JavaScript
tutorials.summary: The language of interactive pages, APIs, and most workshop demos.
tutorials.lede: Browser and Node scripting — fetch, events, and tiny projects.

tutorials.title: Python
tutorials.summary: A readable language for scripting, data work, automation, and teaching.
tutorials.lede: Official tutorial, Automate the Boring Stuff, and Python Koans.

tutorials.title: Lua
tutorials.summary: A small, fast language used in games, mods, Nginx, and other host apps.
tutorials.lede: Try Lua Missions and Programming in Lua after the official getting-started page.

tutorials.title: Git
tutorials.summary: Install, first commit, and the mental model of commits, branches, and remotes.
tutorials.lede: Complete-beginner resources, plus a live Git for Beginners workshop.

tutorials.title: Ruby
tutorials.summary: Expressive OOP and the original Ruby Koans path — learn by failing tests.
tutorials.lede: Ruby in Twenty Minutes, Try Ruby in the browser, then koans.

tutorials.title: Java
tutorials.summary: A widely taught, class-based language that runs on the JVM.
tutorials.lede: Oracle tutorials, Java Koans, and Exercism for drills.

tutorials.title: C++
tutorials.summary: High-performance programming for games, systems, and embedded work.
tutorials.lede: Modern C++ is not “C with classes” — start at isocpp.org and LearnCpp.com.

tutorials.title: Rust
tutorials.summary: Speed and memory safety without a garbage collector — rustup, cargo, and The Book.
tutorials.lede: Rustlings is the community koan: fix small exercises until they compile.

tutorials.title: Writing WordPress Pages
tutorials.summary: Create, edit, and publish pages in the block editor — hierarchy, menus, and clear content.
tutorials.lede: Pages vs posts, the block editor, and how to ship an About or Hours page without fighting the CMS.
